mainText: This is Dose of Good for Wednesday, November 18. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Brazil keeps its measles-free status as others lose theirs. Brazil retains its PAHO-recognised elimination status. It has had 70 cases in 2026, 99.7% fewer than the 2019 peak, and distributed over 16 million vaccine doses to states. Second: Community guardians help Zimbabwe villages live alongside lions. Local people trained as guardians warn when lions approach and help protect livestock. In the first two wards, conflicts fell 98% in about five years; in Mbire and Binga, by 53%. Third: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, 49 years after launch. Launched in 1977, NASA's probe is the first human-made object to reach about 25.9 billion km away: light takes a full day to make the trip. Fourth: Earthshot Prize celebrates solutions to repair the planet. Winners include Denmark's Ørsted, which swapped oil for over 11 GW of offshore wind, the PFAS-Free France campaign with 140,000 supporters, Bhutan and an ocean-protection effort in Niue. Fifth: Agreement secures land for 139 families after a 23-year dispute in Brazil. Families at the former Fazenda da Prata settlement received use contracts for 2,937 hectares. They can now access credit for farming and housing, and say they no longer fear eviction. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
